ai.description: The Green Turtle reaches 1.5 meters in length. It features a heart-shaped carapace with olive-brown hues and a single pair of prefrontal scales on the head. It lacks overlapping scutes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Green Turtle is best distinguished by having only one pair of prefrontal scales on its head, whereas other sea turtles in India possess two pairs.
ai.habitat: Green turtles in the Indian subcontinent inhabit shallow coastal waters, lagoons, and seagrass meadows, nesting on sandy beaches across the mainland and island archipelagos.
ai.behavior: Green turtles are primarily diurnal, spending their days foraging on seagrass and algae before retreating to rocky ledges or coral reefs to rest at night.
ai.reproductionNotes: Green turtles are oviparous, nesting primarily from July to December. They lay multiple clutches per season, averaging 100–120 eggs per nest on Indian beaches.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Chelonia mydas* inhabits coastal waters and nesting beaches across the Indian subcontinent, primarily along the coasts of Gujarat, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, and island territories.
